h1: deVloft Hotel Korat — a central Korat boutique that's just a few minutes' walk from The Mall
intro: Picture this: a small, clean, modern-styled hotel tucked down a quiet lane in central Korat, yet just a few minutes' walk from The Mall Korat with its department store, cinema, and full lineup of restaurants — deVloft Hotel Korat (formerly deVloft Residence) is a small 3-star boutique hotel in Nai Mueang sub-district, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, open since 2020. It has become a popular pick for budget travellers who want a mall-side location · 60 clean, modern air-conditioned rooms, buffet breakfast, a lounge bar, free parking, and a 24-hour front desk · from about THB 700/night · averaging around 8.6 from real reviews on Trip.com, Agoda, and Booking.com.

body.html: Who deVloft Hotel Korat is for — the shortest way to put it: deVloft Hotel Korat is a hotel for people who want a central, mall-side location in Korat without paying a lot and without ending up in a cramped guesthouse room · it isn't a luxury resort by Khao Yai, and it isn't a big chain hotel with a rooftop pool or spa, but a small boutique hotel of about 60 rooms set on Trok Samrong Chan, Nai Mueang sub-district, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima — a spot just a few minutes' walk from The Mall Korat, the city's main shopping centre · the hotel was originally called deVloft Residence before becoming deVloft Hotel Korat, open since 2020, which makes it a newer building compared with many of the city's other budget hotels · it's still open today and scores well within its price bracket, averaging around 8.6 from real reviews on Trip.com, Agoda, and Booking.com · real reviews agree on who fits here: budget travellers, couples on short trips, people stopping over en route to Khao Yai or deeper Isan, and people with business in town who want a stay near the mall for easy shopping and eating · another group that calls it good value is self-drivers, since there's free parking and it's an easy spot for getting on and off the city's main roads · in short, this is a hotel that plays mostly on "a good location at a light price," trading off luxury facilities like a pool or a big fitness centre — something most guests are fine with given the price and the location.

Location and getting around — this is deVloft Hotel Korat's number-one selling point, no question · the hotel sits on Trok Samrong Chan, Nai Mueang sub-district, a small lane in central Korat · the biggest draw is that you can walk to The Mall Korat shopping centre in about 5–6 minutes because it's only about 180–400 metres away — which means meals, the cinema, the supermarket, coffee shops, and convenience stores are all within walking distance, and you never need to call a ride to go out to eat or shop · the area also has plenty of local Korat markets and restaurants to try · longer trips are convenient too: the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo), the city's signature landmark and check-in spot, is about a 10 min drive away, Wat Sala Loi is about a 10 min drive, and Chumphon Gate and the old-town quarter aren't far either · Nakhon Ratchasima railway station is about 1.6 kilometres away, and the bus terminal is just a few minutes' ride, which suits people travelling by train or coach · for self-drivers, the hotel is well placed for getting on and off Mittraphap Road and the city's main roads, and there's free parking · one honest note: the hotel is down a small lane with a fairly narrow access road, so larger vehicles or anyone unfamiliar with the area may need GPS and a slow, careful drive into the soi.

"Chose this place because the walk to The Mall is easy — going out for food and shopping is so convenient, no need to call a ride · clean room, comfy bed, helpful staff · great value for this central a location."

Room types and decor — deVloft Hotel Korat has about 60 rooms, air-conditioned and decorated in a simple, easy-on-the-eye modern tone · they come in several types to suit your group size and budget, starting with the Deluxe Double Room, a Queen-bed room for couples or solo travellers, and the Deluxe Twin Room with two single beds for friends or colleagues · for families there's the Deluxe Family Room that sleeps several people, plus a Deluxe Connecting Room for groups who want adjoining rooms that link together · every room is non-smoking, has a window, and comes with the basic essentials — air-con, fridge, minibar, tea/coffee maker, flat-screen cable TV, free drinking water, and an en-suite bathroom with shower, toiletries, and a hairdryer · from real reviews, most guests agree the rooms are clean, roomier than expected for the price, and the beds are comfortable · the decor looks new and tidy because the building only opened in 2020, so it feels fresher than many of the city's older budget hotels · some room types have a small balcony or sitting nook, and some rooms are advertised as having a pool/pond view outside · but to be straight with you, a few reviews do mention stains or marks in some bathrooms and room quality that may not be consistent across every room — something you can fix by asking to change rooms at check-in if you spot anything off.

Facilities — let's be straight from the start: deVloft Hotel Korat is a small boutique hotel, so there's no swimming pool and no large fitness centre like at a resort or chain hotel · the appeal here isn't luxury facilities but a solid set of genuinely usable basics and a good location · what you do get is a restaurant serving buffet breakfast daily, a lounge bar, free private parking, free Wi-Fi in public areas, laundry service, room service, a convenience corner/shop, a small meeting room, and a 24-hour front desk · the 24-hour desk helps a lot for anyone arriving late, travelling by train or coach in the evening, or needing to set off again before dawn · what nicely makes up for the lack of a pool and gym is the location, since The Mall Korat is within walking distance — anyone wanting to exercise or find entertainment can simply walk over and use the facilities at the mall · overall, deVloft's facilities are "right-sized for the price" — nothing beyond what's needed, but everything you need for a comfortable overnight stay is there.

Food and bar — the hotel has an on-site restaurant serving buffet breakfast daily in the morning (around 6:00 AM–10:00 AM) · from real reviews, the breakfast earns fair praise for the range of options given the room price, with both Thai dishes and basic international items to choose from — a good start to the day before heading out to sightsee or run errands · but some reviews note that the quantity and variety may not match a big-hotel buffet, which is understandable for a small hotel in this price range · besides the restaurant there's also a lounge bar for a relaxed evening drink in a laid-back setting · the biggest help when it comes to food is the hotel's own location, because a few minutes' walk to The Mall Korat puts you within reach of a food court, chain restaurants, coffee shops, and a full supermarket, and the area around the hotel has local Korat restaurants and markets to try — so most guests have breakfast at the hotel and head out for their other meals, which is part of the charm of staying central like this · overall, food isn't a reason to come and eat at deVloft itself, but it's a decent extra that gets your day off to an easy start.

Service — service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews, and it may be the strongest thing about this place aside from the location · several staff are mentioned as friendly, smiling, helpful, and happy to give recommendations on where to eat, what to see, getting around, and calling a ride · the 24-hour front desk makes things much easier for people arriving late or leaving before dawn, which matters for a city that's a stopover point like Korat · check-in and check-out are mostly smooth and quick according to reviews · but to be straight, as a small hotel with a limited team, some standards may not be as polished as a big chain hotel's — response times during busy periods can slow down a bit, and some extra services found at larger hotels may not be available · overall, the warmth and goodwill of the team are what leave many guests impressed, and one reason this place keeps a solid review score.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulled together from Trip.com, Agoda, and Booking.com, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the central, walk-to-The-Mall-Korat location is the single most-mentioned thing, along with rooms that are clean and roomier than expected for the price, a fresh-looking new building since it only opened in 2020, comfortable beds, friendly and helpful staff, a breakfast with a fair range of options, free parking, and great value within its bracket — reviews rate the location especially highly, with many couples giving their two-person trips very strong scores · On the watch-outs side: the two most-mentioned issues are noise and parking — the hotel is central and near restaurants with live music, and some reviews say they could hear music from nearby venues until late (some say until around 1 AM), especially on Friday and Saturday nights · for parking, some note there's limited space when the hotel is full, since it's down a small lane · next is stains or marks in some bathrooms and room quality that may not be consistent across every room · most of these complaints can be eased by asking for a quieter inner room, requesting a room change if you spot anything off, and checking about parking in advance, rather than being big problems that keep most people from coming back.

"Room was clean and new, staff were lovely and really helpful, easy to walk to the mall and find food · the only downside was Saturday night, when music from a nearby venue carried on until late — next time I'll ask for a quieter inner room. Otherwise great value for this location."

Price and value — the starting price for the smallest rooms like the Deluxe Double / Deluxe Twin is about THB 700/night on regular weekdays (around USD 21–26 as shown on the OTAs), and can climb to roughly THB 1,000–1,300+ on weekends, long holidays, or when there's an event in town · larger rooms like the Deluxe Family and Deluxe Connecting Room run higher depending on group size and size · compared with hotels of the same level in Korat, deVloft Hotel Korat feels great value among budget stays that focus on a central, mall-side location · what makes it worthwhile is getting a clean room in a 2020 building, buffet breakfast, free parking, and a location that saves both time and transport costs since you can walk to The Mall yourself · if you're coming to Korat for an overnight stopover, errands, or in-town sightseeing using the hotel as a base, every baht you spend on this location is well returned · but if you expect a pool, a full gym, or the total quiet of an out-of-town resort, this price honestly reflects the trade-off of being a small central hotel without luxury facilities and with some city noise in return.

Good to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, specify at booking that you'd like an inner room not facing the street or next to a restaurant with live music, because the hotel is central and some nights there's music from nearby venues until late — bringing earplugs gives extra peace of mind · two, if you're driving, the upside is free parking, but space is limited and it's down a small lane, so ask about availability ahead and use GPS to drive slowly into the soi · three, at check-in give the bathroom a quick look, and if you find stains or anything off, just ask to change rooms, since room quality may not be consistent · four, make the most of the location by walking to The Mall Korat to eat, shop, and catch a movie instead of calling a ride · five, on long holidays and during events in town, Korat hotels fill up fast and prices rise, so book ahead and compare across platforms · six, pick free cancellation if your plans aren't firm, since prices tend to shift by season.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, deVloft Hotel Korat is the best fit for budget travellers who want a central Korat location within walking distance of The Mall, in a clean room in a new building, with breakfast and free parking, for high-hundreds to low-thousand baht · the walk-to-The-Mall-Korat location, the clean and new-looking rooms (it only opened in 2020), the friendly staff, and the overall value give it a solid review score and make it a popular pick for people stopping over in town · if you're after a pool, a full gym, total quiet, or a luxury resort in nature, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a garden-wrapped boutique like Koranaree Courtyard on a quiet soi, or big central chain hotels like Centara Korat and Kantary Hotel Korat instead · but for a Korat trip where you want a good mall-side location, a clean room, and money left over to make the most of your travels — deVloft Hotel Korat answers that need squarely, which is why it has kept a good score within its price bracket all along.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — deVloft Hotel Korat, Korat

faq.q: Where is deVloft Hotel Korat, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: The hotel is on Trok Samrong Chan, Nai Mueang sub-district, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, in central Korat · the standout is that you can walk to The Mall Korat in 5–6 minutes (about 180–400 m away) — eat, shop, and catch a movie without calling a ride · Nakhon Ratchasima railway station is about 1.6 km away, and the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo) and Wat Sala Loi are about a 10 min drive.

faq.q: How much does deVloft Hotel Korat start at, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 700/night for the Deluxe Double / Deluxe Twin Room on regular weekdays · they climb to THB 1,000–1,300+ on weekends, long holidays, or during events in town · there are also Deluxe Family Room and Deluxe Connecting Room options for families and groups · always compare across several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is deVloft Hotel Korat best for?
faq.a: A great fit for budget travellers, couples, people on an overnight stopover, and those with business in town who want a stay near the mall · clean rooms in a new building, a walk to The Mall Korat, and free parking · if you're after a pool and a full gym, look at Centara Korat or Kantary Hotel Korat, and if you want a quiet garden-wrapped boutique, look at Koranaree Courtyard.

faq.q: What's the noise like at deVloft Hotel Korat, and which room should I ask for?
faq.a: Many reviews agree the hotel is central and near restaurants with live music, and some nights you can hear music until late, especially on Friday and Saturday nights · if you're a light sleeper, it's best to ask for an inner room not facing the street or restaurants at booking, and bring earplugs for extra peace of mind.

faq.q: Does deVloft Hotel Korat have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: The hotel is a small boutique, so there's no swimming pool and no large fitness centre · but there is buffet breakfast daily (around 6:00 AM–10:00 AM) with a fair range of options, a lounge bar, free parking, free Wi-Fi, laundry service, room service, and a 24-hour front desk · anyone wanting to exercise or find more entertainment can walk over to The Mall Korat.

faq.q: What was deVloft Hotel Korat called before, and how long has it been open?
faq.a: The hotel was originally called deVloft Residence before becoming deVloft Hotel Korat · it has been open since 2020, making it a newer building compared with many of the city's budget hotels, which is why real reviews praise the rooms for looking fresh and clean.
